scope: Official XMOS, Seeed Studio, and ReSpeaker upstream sources checked for hardware or firmware newer than the SOPHY-AGI snapshots.

conclusion.summary: XVF3800 remains XMOS's current four-microphone VocalFusion processor. The meaningful updates are newer ReSpeaker firmware, a modular XVF3800-based Flex board, and a separate XCORE-VOICE/XU316 two-microphone platform.
conclusion.immediate_action: Keep the first-pass USB telemetry code, test installed firmware, and evaluate upgrade to ReSpeaker USB 2.1.0 before enabling writes or DFU.
conclusion.hardware_action: Document reSpeaker Flex as the preferred mechanical alternative when array/core separation is valuable.

usb_changes: 2.0.10 restores USB audio state after bus-speed changes and fixes Linux isochronous EOVERFLOW capture failures.
2.0.10 keeps DoA state current regardless of the active LED effect.
2.1.0 adds independent direct-output routing for USB channels 3 through 6.
2.1.0 adds runtime and persistent AIC3104 headphone and line-output level control.
i2s_changes: 1.0.8 aligns DOA_VALUE at command 18 and LED_RING_COLOR at command 19 with the USB interface.
1.0.8 keeps DoA and speech-detection telemetry current regardless of LED effect.

firmware_delta.compatibility_effect: The curated read-only USB DOA_VALUE implementation remains compatible. I2S integrations should require 1.0.8 or explicitly map older command IDs.

candidates.name: reSpeaker Flex XVF3800
candidates.relationship: Newer modular carrier and array architecture using the same XVF3800 processing generation.

candidates.name: ReSpeaker Lite / XCORE-VOICE XU316
candidates.relationship: Complementary two-microphone open voice platform, not an XVF3800 successor.
candidates.disposition: Consider only for a secondary low-power wake/event node.

candidates.name: XMOS XK-VOICE-SQ66
candidates.relationship: XVF3800 evaluation and custom-array development kit.
candidates.disposition: Useful as a reference or firmware-development fixture, not a compact production ear.
